title: 8 משחקים וספרים שיעזרו להם להמציא סיפורים

stage.need: Imagination and making up stories at around ages 6 to 8. CDC 5 years milestone: 'Tells a story she heard or made up with at least two events' and the tips to encourage pretend play and keep a box of materials for creative play; KidsHealth (Storytelling): 'After exposing your child to many ways of storytelling, encourage kids to come up with their own story ... This builds strong communication, organization, and creativity'. Games with picture cards, dice or drawing give a reason to invent, books give worlds to carry on.
stage.age_caveat: Ages are approximate: CDC milestones are what most children (75% or more) do by an age, not a deadline, and the CDC page stops at 5 years, so for 6 to 8 the carousel leans on KidsHealth's storytelling page. Some children invent stories freely and some need more time; the frame says בסביבות and the caption says יש ילדים ש.... Weekly batch 2026-10-18, slot 4, second carousel.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early. (date reviewed 16 May 2026)
dev_sources.quote: Follows rules or takes turns when playing games with other children / Tells a story she heard or made up with at least two events. For example, a cat was stuck in a tree and a firefighter saved it / Teach your child to follow rules in games. For example, play simple board games, card games, or Simon Says. / Encourage your child to pretend play. Help your child find items she can use to play dress up, school, or house. / Keep a box of crayons, paper, paint, child scissors, and glue for creative play.
dev_sources.supports: 5 year milestones and tips: following rules or taking turns in games with other children, telling a story she heard or made up, playing simple board and card games, pretend play and creative play. Read today through a page fetch (the CDC site blocks plain curl); sentences quoted as returned and joined with ' / '. Milestones are what most children do by that age, not a deadline.

dev_sources.title: Storytelling
dev_sources.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (medically reviewed by Kandia N. Lewis, PhD, date reviewed May 2022)
dev_sources.quote: Older kids love a funny twist, so take a favorite story and turn it upside down by changing the setting, characters, or plot. / Encourage your child to tell a story too! After exposing your child to many ways of storytelling, encourage kids to come up with their own story. It's important that kids have the chance to use their imagination to develop ideas and create a story. This builds strong communication, organization, and creativity.
dev_sources.supports: Older children enjoy a story with a twist, and being encouraged to make up their own story gives them a chance to use their imagination; KidsHealth says it builds communication, organization and creativity. A parent explainer, not a test of any product; our copy says practise, never a promised result.

dev_sources.title: The Magic of Play: How It Inspires & Aids Early Development
dev_sources.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (medically reviewed by KidsHealth Medical Experts)
dev_sources.quote: Pretend play lets kids try out new roles for themselves (like superheroes, princesses, dinosaurs, wild animals, or even parents) and allows for creative problem-solving. / Read to your child. And while reading, ask mind-opening questions: "If you were the caterpillar, what would you eat?" and "What do you think will happen next in the story?" This not only encourages imagination but promotes language skills and fosters an interest in books.
dev_sources.supports: Pretend play lets children try new roles and solve problems creatively, and mind-opening questions while reading encourage imagination. The page is about preschoolers; for 6 to 8 it supports the habit (questions while reading) and not an age claim.

image.rights_note: LumeBook's own catalogue cover art for book 49, the 'girl' variant URL, AVIF converted to PNG with ffmpeg without changes.
image.depicts: A small girl with a bob haircut looks up in wonder at a glowing model of the solar system on a stand, with a lit sun and planets orbiting it, in a dark room with faint star charts behind her; her galaxy-print T-shirt has no words. That is the idea of getting a magic model of the solar system. The cover does not show the journey itself, so the line says the children get a magic model and set out on a space adventure. No lettering on the cover. The boy variant (a teenager with a constellation sweater holding the model) was also viewed; the girl variant shows the orbiting planets and the wonder more clearly.

lumebook.connection: Second to last of 8 suggestions (3 games, 4 books and the LumeBook book), between a book and a book, in Yarin's format. Book 49 (ages 4 to 8, category adventures and imagination: a magic model of the solar system takes the child on a journey through the planets) fits a carousel about imagination; the line says what the cover and the site show.
